note: Cases mirror closed_circuit.rs validate_page_content_ownership and validate_second_content_body, with page_content_owner.rs resolve_page_content_owner and reduce_to_owners: embed graphs from @trait tokens (full and config-channel minus overlay-only embeds), the client-bound closure, content-grade main writers (string payloads, children, entity-kind patterns, a false if branch skipped) and the designation/containment reduction, each with paired controls. Each case carries the LINT_INDEX roots of the traits that embed and the pattern registry kinds the content-grade test reads. Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion the Rust validator reports for the same program.

findings.message: page "/p": A, B each render a content body into slot 'main' and none composes the others — the page has no single content owner, so a shell that designates one turns the rest into second bodies
findings.suggestion: make one trait the page's composer — it embeds the others (<trait.X/> or @trait.X in its render) — and mount only it on the page; candidates: A, B

findings.message: page "/p": B renders a content body into slot 'main' while A already owns this page's content — a second, stacked UI if this is not a deliberate dedicated-feature page
findings.suggestion: embed <trait.B> in the composer's render or a config slot (contentTrait/idleContent), or remove B from the page decl if it only hosts dialogs/logic
